citation.title: Denoising diffusion algorithm for inverse design of microstructures with fine-tuned nonlinear material properties
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering, 413, 116126

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The diffusion model generates microstructures conditioned on target nonlinear properties, but the paper does not compare its outcome with a classical optimization method.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical-versus-ML speed comparison or derivable speed-up is reported.
claim.alternatives: The introduction describes conventional optimization as difficult and motivates machine learning, but does not report a classical comparator's cost or result.

baseline.quality_metric: Target hyperelastic energy response and topology features; predicted by CNN surrogate

notes: The article introduces a diffusion generator and CNN surrogate but reports no classical method run, timing, or classical result used as a comparator. Its discussion of conventional optimization as generally difficult is motivation only. Full text read from the public-access repository copy: https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10487106.
